answer: Before any work, each identity must rent its own question batch from an outside data vendor. A batch costs money and is watermarked: a unique ordering plus small numeric perturbations that resurface in the mistakes its user makes. Pay settles later against a holdout set no buyer sees, so reselling a batch yields no extra accuracy, and two submissions sharing one watermark forfeit both bonds. A hollow account cannot bridge itself to data for free: a thousand clones mean a thousand purchases at its real marginal price, each traceable. An orchard is worth the harvest nobody can borrow.
